WindowsCraft 0.15.2 (screens, in-game monitors, gaming monitors and tablets for Cobbleverse)

New in 0.15.7: windows you share on a wall (not just in-game monitors) now also use direct GPU
sharing with Sodium; with 0.15.6 they could still fall back to copying through the CPU. While
nobody is watching a screen you share, your PC no longer keeps making full-size copies of it for
a stream that's paused. Servers with a server-ip set open WindowsCraft's relay on that address only.

New in 0.15.6: direct GPU sharing now works with Sodium. Sodium's "no error" OpenGL mode (on by
default) hid a mistake that made the shared pictures come out black, so WindowsCraft turned GPU
sharing off and copied every picture through the CPU instead. Measured with a 4K in-game monitor
in the Cobbleverse modpack (Iris + Solas): the game went from 37 to 89 frames a second, the
monitor from 22 to 52 pictures a second, and the picture's delay from ~100 ms to a few ms. If
your PC had decided "black" before, it tests again by itself.

New in 0.15.5: when someone you allowed uses one of your in-game monitors, their clicks and keys
reach it the moment they arrive, instead of waiting for your game to draw its next frame (measured:
a click took about 21 ms to reach the app with your game at 30 frames a second; now about 3 ms),
and finding the window under their click never makes your game stutter. And when someone's screen
had a hiccup in its sound, the extra sound kept to bridge the next one (and with it the picture,
which waits for the sound) is given back once things have been steady for a couple of minutes.

New in 0.15.4: fixes 0.15.3 restarting the stream of a screen you share every few seconds while
your own wall of it looked small (the people watching saw it pause and fall behind). Sitting down
at one of your screens brings its full-size picture back at once. The Windows self-test no longer
opens Task Manager on PCs where Windows starts it as administrator (it then stayed in front and
spoiled the tests after it).

New in 0.15.3: Settings -> Performance is Automatic (WindowsCraft decides, and says what it's
doing right now) or Advanced (pick each setting yourself); settings you had turned off stay off.
Each of your screens can have its own picks on its Picture page. New and on by Automatic: your
own walls get a smaller copy of a big screen while it looks small from where you are (a 4K
in-game monitor across the room was copied in full 20 times a second; now it keeps up and the
game runs smoother). Full size as you come closer or sit down; what others see never changes.

New in 0.15.2: someone else's screen shows each change the moment it arrives (the last change
before a screen went still could wait for the next one), its pictures are coloured by the
graphics card (less work for the PC watching), and a movie on it plays with its sound in step
while you just watch (the picture takes the quickest way again the moment you use the screen).
WindowsCraft now uses one tested FFmpeg version (fetched once more in the background if yours is
older), and direct GPU sharing double-checks before it decides it doesn't work on your PC.

New in 0.15.1: the sound of a screen you share now reaches the people watching (on Windows most
of it was lost on the way); someone who starts watching gets the full frame rate (they were
dropped to 30 a second by mistake); your own walls get each picture sooner, and the people
watching see your screen about a third sooner (more on a screen that changes slowly); a screen you aren't
looking at no longer costs your PC the work of its picture (its sound keeps playing). And
"/windowscraft measure start 60" measures for a minute what your screens cost and how long each
step takes (off unless you start it; the report lands in windowscraft/measurements).

1. Close Minecraft.
2. Right-click this zip and choose "Extract All...", then open the extracted folder.
3. Double-click "Install WindowsCraft.bat".
   If Windows says "Windows protected your PC": click "More info", then "Run anyway".
4. Start Cobbleverse and join the server as usual.

The server needs this version too: put the same windowscraft .jar into the server's "mods"
folder (delete the old windowscraft .jar there) and restart it. Anyone already on 0.14.2 or
newer is offered this update in chat when they join, and it updates itself (anyone older than
0.14.2 installs it by hand once, like this).

U anywhere: the WindowsCraft menu - all your screens (what's open on them, who can use them,
their size and picture) and the settings.
In-game monitor: look at a black concrete wall or a gaming monitor block and press U (the first
time it offers to install a free display driver). Press O to sit down and use it with your real
mouse and keyboard - it's then shown flat and sharp on your screen like a real monitor, as big
as fits in what you see of the game (never under your taskbar), with the room around it (Alt +
scroll out: still sharp, just smaller); Esc gets up.
Hold Alt and look at your monitor to point and click on it without sitting down.
An app that only runs once (Discord, Calculator...) already open on your desk: opening it from a
monitor brings it over, in the middle of that monitor (and opening it from your own taskbar brings
it back). Each monitor plays only its own sound, never mixed: U on a monitor -> "Own copies of apps" -> Set up
(free Sandboxie-Plus, installed hidden; Windows asks once). Then every app you start at that monitor
is its own copy: its own sound, its own logins (sign in once there, it stays). Your desk's apps are
never touched; Discord and WhatsApp come over instead. Full-screen videos stay full screen when you
press Esc. U again turns it off; sneak + U opens its menu.
Gaming monitors and tablets: creative tab "WindowsCraft" (or craft them). A gaming monitor faces
you when placed (8 directions). Placed right beside, above or below another one it joins it (no
stand, edge to edge, turned to face you - stand at your seat while placing; sneak to keep it flat)
- joined monitors are joined in Windows too, so windows drag across them.
Each screen's volume (0-500 %): U menu, the slider under its name.
A tablet: holding it turns it on; right-click holds it up (it fills your screen), Esc puts it
down (it keeps playing in your hand), sneak + right-click turns it off.
To share a window or your screen instead: sneak + U on a wall, pick one, Go Live.
On someone else's screen, U opens listening options (3D or direct sound, volume, mute).
Press O while looking at a live screen for theater mode.

If U does nothing or in-game monitors won't turn on: the display driver got stuck. WindowsCraft
now notices that and offers "Repair driver" (Windows asks for permission). Restarting the PC
fixes it too.
If something else about in-game monitors misbehaves: close Minecraft, open the "Windows self-test"
folder and double-click "Run self-test.bat". It takes a couple of minutes (your screens blink and
the mouse moves - leave the PC alone meanwhile) and puts "WindowsCraft self-test" on your desktop:
send that folder's report.
